Amazon.cares: Cost, ownership and what happens when a dependency fails. Name managed services and say how you'd operate them.
dives: How would you cut the running cost of this in half?
Right-size with autoscaling, move cold data to cheaper storage tiers, cache hot reads, use spot or Graviton instances for workers, and drop over-provisioned replicas.
A dependency in one Availability Zone goes down. What happens?
Run every tier across 3 AZs behind a load balancer, keep services stateless, use timeouts, retries with jitter and circuit breakers, and fail over the database automatically.

Google.cares: Huge scale, clean estimates and consistency trade-offs. Show the numbers drive the design.
dives: Traffic grows 100x. What breaks first and how do you shard?
The single database and hot keys break first. Shard by a high-cardinality key with consistent hashing, add caches in front, and split read and write paths.
Strong or eventual consistency here, and why?
Strong only where users would notice (money, uniqueness, ownership); eventual everywhere else for latency and availability, with idempotent writes to make retries safe.

Meta.cares: Product sense, fast iteration and fan-out to billions of users. Start from the user experience.
dives: How would you roll out a change to this safely to 3 billion users?
Feature flags, a dark launch, then 1% to 10% to 100% with dashboards and automatic rollback on error or latency regressions.
Where does fan-out hurt, and how do you tame it?
Write fan-out explodes for huge audiences: switch to pull for big accounts, batch writes, and cache the merged result.

Microsoft.cares: Enterprise needs: identity, multi-tenancy, compliance and reliability SLAs.
dives: How do you isolate tenants?
Tenant id on every row and request, per-tenant quotas, and dedicated cells for the biggest customers; never share caches across tenants without the tenant in the key.
What SLA can you promise and how do you meet it?
99.9% needs multi-AZ and automated failover; 99.99% needs multi-region active-active, health checks and tested runbooks.

Uber.cares: Realtime data, geography and staying up during spikes.
dives: Demand spikes 10x at 6 pm in one city. What happens?
Partition by city or geo-cell so the spike stays local, autoscale that cell, shed low-priority work and protect the core write path.
How do you handle a region going dark mid-trip?
Replicate trip state across regions, let clients reconnect to the next region, and make every state change idempotent so retries are safe.

Stripe.cares: Correctness above all: idempotency, exactly-once effects and an audit trail.
dives: A request times out. Did it happen or not?
Every write carries an idempotency key; retry with the same key and the server returns the first result instead of acting twice.
How do you prove the numbers are right?
Append-only, double-entry records, daily reconciliation against the source of truth, and alerts on any mismatch.

Apple.cares: Privacy, on-device work and a smooth experience on flaky networks.
dives: What can run on the device instead of the server?
Caching, ranking and some ML can run on-device; send only what the server truly needs, encrypted, and sync when the network is good.
How do you keep user data private?
Collect the minimum, encrypt in transit and at rest, end-to-end where possible, and keep identifiers out of logs and analytics.

modern: Edge redirects
Serve hot redirects from edge functions and an edge key-value cache (Cloudflare Workers KV, CloudFront Functions) so most clicks never reach your region.
Serverless key-value store
A managed KV store (DynamoDB, Bigtable) partitioned by code replaces a self-run cluster.
Streaming analytics
Click events go to a managed stream and land in a lakehouse (Iceberg) for analytics instead of nightly batch jobs.
Safety
Scan new URLs against threat-intel APIs before they go live; phishing abuse is the top real-world risk.

extra.look: Shorteners are a favourite for phishing. They want you to think about abuse before scale.
rounds: How do you stop people shortening phishing links?
Check new URLs against Safe Browsing / threat-intel APIs and block known-bad domains
Ask users to promise they won't
Someone creates millions of links a minute. What do you do?
Rate limit creation per user and IP, require auth for bulk use
A link turns malicious after creation. Now what?
Re-scan popular links, let users report, and show an interstitial warning page

scenarios.name: Big Tech scale
scenarios.blurb: Billions of clicks a day across every continent.
scenarios.lens: Global latency, multi-region and hot links.
reqN: Redirect under 20 ms worldwide
Survive a full region outage
est: Reads: 1M/s at peak, mostly a few hot links

blocks.edge: Hot redirects answered at the edge, close to the user.
blocks.rep: Every region has a replica so redirects survive a region outage.

dives: One link goes viral: 1M clicks a second. What happens?
It's served from the edge cache and the in-region Redis; origin sees almost none of it. Pre-warm the edge for known campaigns.
wrap: Next: geo-routed DNS and per-region write ownership for custom aliases.

scenarios.name: Startup MVP
scenarios.blurb: Ship in a week, a few thousand users, tiny budget.
scenarios.lens: Simplicity and cost: the smallest thing that works and can grow.
reqN: Costs a few dollars a month
One person can run it
est: Writes: ~10/s at most; one Postgres handles it easily

blocks.pg: One managed Postgres holds links and clicks until scale demands more.

dives: Why not start with Kafka and a KV store?
You don't need them yet. One Postgres with an index on code serves thousands of redirects a second; add pieces when numbers say so.
wrap: First thing to add when traffic grows: Redis for hot codes.

modern: Edge and gateway limits
Most teams use the API gateway's built-in limiter (Envoy, Kong, API Gateway) or edge WAF rules before writing their own.
Token-aware limits for AI
AI APIs limit by tokens per minute and concurrent requests, not just request count.
Adaptive limits
Limits adjust to backend health (load shedding) instead of fixed numbers.

extra.look: Real limiters protect paying customers first. Show you think in plans and priorities.
rounds: Free and paid users share the API. How do limits differ?
Per-plan rules: higher limits and burst for paid tiers, separate buckets per API key
The backend is overloaded but no user is over limit. What now?
Load shedding: drop or queue low-priority traffic first
How do clients know when to retry?

scenarios.name: AI API (tokens)
scenarios.blurb: Limit an LLM API where one request can cost 100x another.
scenarios.lens: Cost per request varies wildly, so count tokens, not calls.
reqF: Limit tokens per minute and concurrent requests per key
est: A request can use 100 to 100,000 tokens: count after the response streams

blocks.tok: Counts tokens per key as responses stream, and debits the bucket.

dives: You don't know the token count until the answer finishes. How do you limit?
Reserve an estimate up front, then settle the real count when the stream ends; cap concurrent requests too.
wrap: Next: per-model limits and priority queues for paying customers.

scenarios.name: Global gateway
scenarios.blurb: Many regions, one limit per customer.
reqN: Limit is global, not per region
No cross-region call on the hot path

blocks.sync: Regions keep local counters and share them every second, so limits are nearly global without a slow call.

dives: Strict global limits need a cross-region call. How do you avoid it?
Split the limit across regions by recent traffic and rebalance every few seconds; accept a small overshoot.
wrap: Trade-off accepted: up to ~5% overshoot for low latency.

modern: Managed realtime
Many teams use managed WebSocket or pub/sub layers (AWS AppSync, Ably, Pusher) or a WebSocket gateway instead of running their own fleet.
End-to-end encryption
Signal protocol style E2EE is expected for consumer chat; the server stores ciphertext.
Cheap storage tiers
Recent messages in a fast store, older history tiered to object storage.
AI features
Smart replies and summaries run as async consumers of the message stream.

extra.look: Chat is a connection problem first. They want to hear how you hold and route millions of sockets.
rounds: How does a message find the server holding B's connection?
A registry (Redis) maps user id to chat server; route through the queue to that server
Store it in the DB and hope
A chat server restarts with 50k connections. What happens?
Clients reconnect with backoff to another server and sync missed messages by last message id
How do you scale to 100M open sockets?
Many stateless connection servers (~50k-100k each) behind a load balancer with sticky routing

scenarios.name: Private messenger (E2EE)
scenarios.blurb: Like Signal or WhatsApp: the server must not read messages.
scenarios.lens: Privacy: keys, devices and what the server can't see.
reqN: Server never sees plaintext
Multi-device support

blocks.keys: Stores each device's public keys so senders can encrypt for every device.

dives: How do group messages work with E2EE?
Sender keys: encrypt once with a group key shared to each member device; rotate it when someone leaves.
wrap: Trade-off: no server-side search or spam scanning of content.

scenarios.name: Workplace chat
scenarios.blurb: Like Slack: channels, threads, search, enterprise customers.

blocks.idx: Messages are indexed from the stream so search stays fresh.

dives: A customer needs 7-year retention and legal hold. How?
Per-tenant retention policies, legal-hold flags that block deletion, and tiered storage for old messages.
wrap: Next: per-tenant encryption keys for enterprise customers.

modern: ML ranking
Feeds are ranked by models in two stages (candidate retrieval, then ranking), not just by time.
Feature store
User and post features served from a low-latency feature store for ranking.
Event streaming
Posts and interactions flow through Kafka for fan-out, ranking signals and analytics.

extra.look: Modern feeds are ranked. They want a simple, staged ranking story.
rounds: How do you pick 20 posts from 10,000 candidates fast?
Two stages: cheap candidate retrieval, then a heavier ranking model on a few hundred
Score all 10,000 with the big model
Engagement history, relationship strength, recency and content type
How do you test a new ranking model?
A/B test on a small slice and watch engagement and quality metrics

scenarios.name: Celebrity scale
scenarios.blurb: Accounts with 100M followers post every hour.
dives: A celebrity posts. Do you write to 100M feeds?
No: pull their posts at read time and merge with the precomputed feed.
wrap: Watch: hot partitions for celebrity posts; replicate them widely.

scenarios.name: Realtime feed
scenarios.blurb: New posts appear live without refresh.

blocks.ws: Pushes a 'new posts' signal to open clients instead of them polling.

dives: Push every new post to every open client?
Push a lightweight 'new posts available' hint; clients fetch when the user scrolls up.
wrap: Trade-off: connection cost versus freshness.

modern: Per-title encoding
Encoding ladders tuned per video (AV1 where supported) cut bandwidth 30-50%.
Managed transcoding
Cloud media services (MediaConvert, Transcoder API) or GPU encoders instead of a self-run farm.
Multi-CDN
Large services steer traffic across several CDNs and their own edge caches (Open Connect style).

extra.look: Bytes are the cost. They want to hear how you get video close to viewers cheaply.
rounds: Where should a popular video's bytes come from?
Edge caches near the viewer, pre-positioned before peak
How do you cut bandwidth without hurting quality?
Per-title encoding and newer codecs like AV1 on supported devices
Playback stutters on mobile. What helps?
Adaptive bitrate with short segments and a sensible starting quality

scenarios.name: Live streaming
scenarios.blurb: Like Twitch: millions watch a stream live.
reqN: Glass-to-glass latency under 5 s

blocks.ing: Takes the live feed and hands short segments to transcoders in real time.

dives: How do you get latency under 5 seconds?
Low-latency HLS or WebRTC, 1-2 s segments, and transcoding as the stream arrives.
wrap: Next: live chat and clips.

scenarios.name: Short video
scenarios.blurb: Like TikTok: short clips, endless scroll.
scenarios.lens: Prefetching and recommendation, not long playback.
dives: How do you make the next video start instantly?
Prefetch the first seconds of the next few recommended clips while the current one plays.
wrap: The recommender is the product: plan its feature pipeline early.

modern: H3 hexagons
Uber's H3 grid is the common choice for geo cells and supply-demand maps.
Cell-based architecture
Cities run in isolated cells so a failure or spike stays local.
Streaming ETA
ETA and pricing models consume live location streams (Kafka + Flink).

extra.look: Location data is huge and short-lived. They want memory, cells and streams.
rounds: Where do live driver locations live?
In memory, indexed by geo cell (Redis GEO or H3)
A SQL table updated every 4 s
How do you find drivers within 2 km?
Look up the rider's cell and its neighbours, then rank by ETA
How does surge pricing get computed?
Stream supply and demand per cell and update prices every minute

scenarios.name: Food delivery
scenarios.blurb: Like Uber Eats: restaurant, courier and customer.
reqF: Track order from restaurant to door

blocks.rest: Restaurants accept orders and share prep time, which decides when to dispatch a courier.

dives: When do you send the courier?
Time dispatch so they arrive as food is ready: predicted prep time minus travel time.
wrap: Next: batching multiple orders per courier.

scenarios.name: Global, many cities
scenarios.blurb: Hundreds of cities, each with its own peaks.
dives: How do you stop one city's spike hurting others?
Partition by city or region into cells with their own capacity and failover.
wrap: Cells make failures local and deploys safer.

modern: Managed providers
Use managed delivery (SNS, Firebase, Twilio, SES) and focus on preferences and routing.
Event-driven triggers
Services publish events; the notification service subscribes, so senders don't call it directly.
Smart delivery
Batching, digests and send-time optimisation reduce noise and opt-outs.

extra.look: Good notification systems send less. They want user trust, not volume.
rounds: A user gets 30 likes in a minute. What do you send?
How do you respect time zones?
Hold non-urgent messages until the user's local quiet hours end
How do you know a channel is working?
Track delivered and opened rates per channel and alert on drops

scenarios.name: Security codes (OTP)
scenarios.blurb: Login codes that must arrive in seconds.
reqN: Delivered in under 5 s
Never queued behind marketing messages

blocks.prio: Urgent messages skip the bulk queues entirely.

dives: The SMS provider is slow. What now?
Fail over to a second provider after a short timeout and offer an app or email fallback.
wrap: Separate urgent from bulk end to end.

scenarios.name: Marketing campaigns
scenarios.blurb: Send 50M messages for a sale tonight.
dives: How do you send 50M without getting blocked?
Throttle to provider limits, spread over time, honour opt-outs and warm up sending domains.
wrap: Next: send-time optimisation per user.

modern: Headless rendering
Many pages need JavaScript: a pool of headless browsers renders the important ones.
Respect AI-crawl rules
Honour robots.txt including AI-bot rules and site licensing signals.
Lakehouse storage
Pages land in compressed columnar storage (WARC + Parquet) for search and AI training pipelines.

extra.look: Crawling is about being a good citizen. They test rules and rate limits.
rounds: How do you avoid overloading a small website?
One queue per host with a delay between requests
A site's robots.txt disallows your bot. What do you do?
Respect it and skip those paths
Crawl anyway with a fake user agent
Pages need JavaScript to show content. What now?
Render a prioritised subset with headless browsers

scenarios.name: AI training data
scenarios.blurb: Collect web text for model training.

blocks.q: Drops low-quality, duplicate and disallowed content before storage.

dives: How do you keep training data clean?
Dedupe near-duplicates, filter by quality scores and licence signals, and strip personal data.
wrap: Next: provenance tracking per document.

scenarios.name: Price monitoring
scenarios.blurb: Re-check 10M product pages every hour.
dives: How do you crawl only what changed?
Re-crawl by change rate: fast-changing pages often, stable ones rarely; use ETags and sitemaps.
wrap: Next: alerts when a tracked price drops.

modern: Orchestration across providers
Route payments across several PSPs for cost, approval rate and failover.
Event-sourced ledger
The ledger is an append-only event log; balances are projections.
Real-time fraud ML
Fraud scoring runs inline in milliseconds using streaming features.
Network tokens
Store network tokens instead of card numbers to cut PCI scope.

extra.look: Money must never be lost or doubled. They push hard on failure cases.
rounds: The provider times out. Did the charge happen?
Unknown: retry with the same idempotency key or query the provider before acting
Assume it failed and charge again
How do you keep the ledger correct?
Double-entry, append-only entries that always balance
Your records and the provider's disagree. What now?
Daily reconciliation flags the mismatch for automatic or manual fix

scenarios.name: Digital wallet
scenarios.blurb: Users hold a balance and send money to each other.
dives: Two transfers spend the same balance at once. How do you stop it?
Atomic debit with a balance check in one transaction (or a per-account lock); the ledger rejects overdrafts.
wrap: Next: compliance checks (KYC, limits).

scenarios.name: Marketplace payouts
scenarios.blurb: Like Uber or Airbnb: collect from buyers, pay sellers.

blocks.po: Pays sellers on a schedule from their ledger balance.

dives: When do sellers get paid?
After a hold period for refunds and disputes, from the ledger balance, in batches.
wrap: Next: currency conversion and tax reporting.

modern: Hybrid suggestions
Combine prefix matches with semantic and personalised suggestions.
Edge caching
Popular prefixes cached at the edge for single-digit milliseconds.
Streaming trends
Trending queries updated in minutes from a stream, not hourly batch.

extra.look: Suggestions must be fast, fresh and safe.
rounds: A news event makes a new query explode. How fast does it show?
Stream recent counts and blend them into suggestions within minutes
How do you stop offensive suggestions?
Filter with blocklists and classifiers before publishing the trie
How do you personalise without slowing down?
Merge a small per-user list with the global top-k at request time

scenarios.name: E-commerce search
scenarios.blurb: Suggest products and categories as you type.
dives: What should rank first: popular queries or products in stock?
Blend popularity with conversion and stock; never suggest out-of-stock items first.
wrap: Next: spelling correction and synonyms.

scenarios.name: AI-assisted search
scenarios.blurb: Suggest full questions, not just words.

blocks.emb: Finds suggestions by meaning when prefixes don't match.

dives: Embedding lookups are slower. When do you use them?
Only when the prefix trie has few results, and cache the answers.
wrap: Watch: latency budget per keystroke.

modern: Content-defined chunking
Chunk boundaries based on content (rolling hash) so an insert doesn't shift every chunk.
Object storage tiers
Cold files move automatically to cheaper storage classes.
Realtime collaboration
Docs use CRDTs or operational transforms; plain files keep conflict copies.

extra.look: Two devices edit offline. They want a clear, safe rule.
rounds: Two laptops edit the same file offline. What happens on sync?
Detect by version; keep both as a conflicted copy
How do you upload only what changed?
Hash chunks and send only the new ones
Upload the whole file every time
How do other devices learn of a change?
Push a notification, then they pull the changed metadata and chunks
Wait for the user to refresh

scenarios.name: Photo backup
scenarios.blurb: Like Google Photos: billions of images.

blocks.th: Makes small previews so browsing never loads full images.

dives: How do you keep storage costs sane?
Dedupe by hash, compress, and tier old originals to cold storage.
wrap: Next: search by what's in the photo.

scenarios.name: Enterprise drive
scenarios.blurb: Shared drives with permissions and audits.
dives: How do you check permissions fast?
Cache effective permissions per user and folder; invalidate on change.
wrap: Next: audit logs and data-loss prevention.

modern: Virtual waiting rooms
Managed queue services (Queue-it, CDN waiting rooms) absorb launch spikes.
Bot protection
Bot detection and verified-fan presales are now standard for hot events.
Short holds in Redis
Seat holds with TTLs plus a DB constraint as the final guard.

extra.look: Hot events attract bots. They want fair access, not just throughput.
rounds: Bots grab all seats in seconds. What helps?
Bot detection, verified-fan presale codes and per-account limits
How do you decide who gets in first?
A virtual queue ordered by arrival (or random for presale)
A buyer's card fails at checkout. What happens to the seats?
The hold is released when it expires or payment fails

scenarios.name: Mega concert on-sale
scenarios.blurb: 2M fans, 60k seats, 10 a.m. Friday.
dives: How many people do you let in at once?
Only as many as the booking path can serve; the waiting room meters the rest.
wrap: Load test at 10x before the on-sale.

scenarios.name: Cinema chain
scenarios.blurb: Thousands of small screens, steady traffic.
dives: Do you need a waiting room here?
Usually not: traffic is steady; a DB unique constraint and short holds are enough.
wrap: Keep it simple: one SQL DB per region.

modern: Managed geo search
Use geo queries in managed stores (PostGIS, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch geo, Redis GEO) before building your own index.
H3 or S2 cells
Hexagonal or spherical cells give even neighbour searches worldwide.
Ranking
Results ranked by distance, rating, open-now and personal taste.

extra.look: They want to hear how a point becomes a fast lookup.
rounds: How do you find places within 2 km fast?
Map the point to a cell and search that cell plus neighbours
Sort the whole table by distance
Ask the map provider each time
Downtown cells hold 10,000 places. What now?
Use smaller cells there (quadtree or finer H3 level)
How fresh must the index be?
New places can wait hours; open-now status is computed at query time

scenarios.name: Nearby friends
scenarios.blurb: Live locations of friends who opted in.

blocks.loc: Friends' latest positions, kept in memory with short TTLs.

dives: How is this different from places?
Points move constantly: keep them in memory, update every few seconds, and only for friends who opted in.
wrap: Privacy first: coarse location by default.

scenarios.name: Delivery radius
scenarios.blurb: Which stores can deliver to this address?
dives: Delivery zones aren't circles. How do you check?
Store zones as polygons and do point-in-polygon on candidates from a cell lookup.
wrap: Next: ETA per store.

modern: Model routing
Route each request to the cheapest model that can handle it, with fallback across providers.
Prompt caching
Provider prompt caching cuts cost and latency for long, repeated system prompts.
Evals in CI
Every prompt or model change runs an eval suite before release.
Tools and memory
Chat apps call tools (search, code) and keep long-term memory.

extra.look: Cost and latency decide AI products. They want routing, caching and limits.
rounds: Most questions are easy. How do you keep cost down?
Route easy prompts to a small model, hard ones to a large one
Your long system prompt costs a lot every turn. What helps?
Prompt caching on the provider side
How do you stop one user running up a huge bill?
Token-based rate limits and budgets per user

scenarios.name: Enterprise assistant
scenarios.blurb: Employees chat over company data.

blocks.rag: Grounds answers in company documents the user is allowed to see.

dives: How do you stop it leaking documents someone can't access?
Filter retrieval by the user's permissions (ACLs) before anything reaches the model.
wrap: Next: audit logs of every answer and source.

scenarios.name: Consumer app at scale
scenarios.blurb: Millions of free users, tight margins.
dives: How do you make free users affordable?
Small models by default, caching, tight token limits, upgrade for heavy use.
wrap: Watch cost per daily active user every week.

modern: Hybrid search + rerank
BM25 plus vectors, then a cross-encoder reranker, is the 2026 default.
Contextual chunks
Add document context to each chunk before embedding to improve recall.
Agentic retrieval
For hard questions, an agent decides what to search and when to stop.
Evals
Measure retrieval recall and answer faithfulness on a fixed question set.

extra.look: RAG fails quietly. They want measurement and guardrails.
rounds: How do you know retrieval is good?
Recall@k on a labelled question set
Ask the model if it's sure
The answer sounds right but isn't in the documents. What do you do?
Check faithfulness and answer 'not found' when context is missing
A user shouldn't see HR documents. How do you enforce it?
Filter retrieval by the user's permissions
Tell the model not to mention them

scenarios.name: Support knowledge base
scenarios.blurb: Answer customers from help articles.
dives: What if the answer isn't in the help centre?
Say so and hand off to a human with the conversation.
wrap: Track deflection rate and wrong-answer reports.

scenarios.name: Legal / regulated docs
scenarios.blurb: Contracts and policies where mistakes are costly.
dives: How do you make answers auditable?
Quote exact passages with document and page, and log every answer with its sources.
wrap: Human review for high-risk answers.

modern: MCP for tools
Tools are exposed through MCP servers so any agent can use them.
Durable execution
Long tasks run on durable workflow engines (Temporal style) so they survive crashes.
Sandboxes
Code and browser actions run in isolated sandboxes.
Tracing and evals
Every step is traced (OpenTelemetry for LLMs) and task success is evaluated.

extra.look: Agents act in the world. They want limits, approvals and recovery.
rounds: An agent wants to delete a production table. What happens?
Risky tools need human approval and least-privilege credentials
Ask the model if it's sure
A task crashes at step 30 of 50. Now what?
Resume from the last saved step; tools are idempotent
Ask the user to redo it
How do you stop runaway loops?
Step, token and time budgets with a stop check

scenarios.name: DevOps agent
scenarios.blurb: An agent that fixes incidents.
dives: What can the agent do without a human?
Read-only diagnosis freely; any change needs approval or runs in a safe, reversible way.
wrap: Next: runbooks as tools.

scenarios.name: Multi-agent team
scenarios.blurb: Several specialist agents working together.

blocks.sup: Splits work and merges results from specialist agents.

dives: When is multi-agent worth it?
When tasks split cleanly into parallel parts with separate context; otherwise one agent is simpler.
wrap: Watch: cost multiplies with each agent.

modern: Agentic search over embeddings
Coding agents mostly search with grep and file tools rather than vector indexes.
Sub-agents
Parallel sub-agents explore in their own context windows.
Hooks and permissions
Policies and hooks gate risky commands.
Background agents
Agents run in cloud sandboxes and open pull requests on their own.

extra.look: Code that compiles isn't done. They want tests and review in the loop.
rounds: How does the agent know its change works?
Run tests and the build before committing
The change touches 40 files. How do you keep it safe?
Small commits, review the diff, and a pull request for human review
The repo is huge. How does it find the right code?
Search with grep and file tools, read only what matters

scenarios.name: Fix failing CI
scenarios.blurb: An agent triggered by a red build.
dives: Can it push the fix itself?
Open a pull request with the failing test now passing; a human merges.
wrap: Track how many agent PRs get merged.

scenarios.name: Large migration
scenarios.blurb: Upgrade a framework across 2,000 files.
dives: How do you split the work?
A plan per module, parallel sub-agents, shared conventions, and tests per batch.
wrap: Ship in batches behind feature flags.

modern: Parallel search agents
A lead agent fans out to parallel searchers with separate contexts.
Citations checked
A final pass verifies every claim against its source.
Budgets
Explicit token, step and time budgets per run.

extra.look: Research is only useful if it's true. They push on sources.
rounds: How do you make sure claims are real?
Every claim must cite a source, and a checker verifies them
Ask the model to be careful
Two sources disagree. What does the report do?
Show both, with which is more reliable and why
How do you keep cost bounded?
Budgets on steps, tokens and time per agent

scenarios.name: Market research
scenarios.blurb: Competitor and market sizing reports.
dives: How do you handle numbers from different years?
Normalise to one year, cite each figure with its date, and flag estimates.
wrap: Next: scheduled refresh of reports.

scenarios.name: Internal knowledge
scenarios.blurb: Research across company docs and tickets.
dives: How do you keep it within what the user can see?
Every search runs with the user's permissions.
wrap: Audit log of sources used.

modern: Agent + tools
Support agents act through tools (refunds, order lookup) with limits, not just answer FAQs.
Voice and chat in one
The same agent logic serves chat, email and voice.
Continuous evals
Conversations are scored automatically for resolution and tone.

extra.look: The best support AI knows when to stop. They test escalation.
rounds: When should the AI hand off to a human?
Low confidence, angry customer, or the customer asks
What does the human see on handoff?
Full conversation, actions taken and a summary
A refund over $500 is requested. What happens?
Above the tool's cap, it needs human approval

scenarios.name: E-commerce
scenarios.blurb: Orders, returns and delivery questions.
dives: Most tickets are 'where is my order'. How do you handle them?
Answer directly from order and tracking tools without a human.
wrap: Next: proactive delay notices.

scenarios.name: Banking
scenarios.blurb: Regulated, sensitive data.
dives: How do you verify the customer before acting?
Authenticated session or step-up verification before any account action.
wrap: Log everything for compliance.

modern: Speech-to-speech models
Realtime models take audio in and out, cutting latency.
WebRTC everywhere
WebRTC transport with server-side voice activity detection.
Telephony bridges
SIP trunks connect phone calls to the same agent.

extra.look: Voice feels broken above a second. They want a latency budget.
rounds: Split it: speech-to-text, model, text-to-speech, network, each streaming
A tool call takes 3 s. What does the caller hear?
A short filler while the tool runs
Voice activity detection stops speech and listens

scenarios.name: Call centre
scenarios.blurb: Thousands of concurrent phone calls.
dives: How do you scale to 5,000 concurrent calls?
Stateless media workers per call, autoscaled, with model capacity reserved for peak.
wrap: Next: warm transfer to human agents.

scenarios.name: In-app voice assistant
scenarios.blurb: Talk to an app on your phone.
dives: The network is poor. What helps?
Adaptive audio codecs, on-device voice detection and short responses.
wrap: Next: on-device wake word.

modern: One gateway for all models
Teams call one gateway that routes to any provider and self-hosted models.
Policy as code
Data and usage rules defined as code and enforced at the gateway.
Cost chargeback
Token usage and cost metered per team in real time.

extra.look: Enterprises buy control. They test policy, audit and cost.
rounds: A team sends customer data to a model. How is it controlled?
PII redaction and data policies enforced at the gateway
Finance asks who spent what. How do you answer?
Per-team metering of tokens and cost
A provider has an outage. What happens?
Route to a fallback provider automatically

scenarios.name: Regulated bank
scenarios.blurb: Strict data residency and audit.
dives: Data must stay in the EU. How?
Route only to EU-hosted models and self-hosted endpoints; block others by policy.
wrap: Next: model approval workflow.

scenarios.name: Fast-moving startup
scenarios.blurb: Many experiments, small team.
dives: How do you let teams try new models fast?
Self-serve keys with budgets and default safety policies.
wrap: Keep the gateway thin and stateless.

modern: Agent over the data
An analytics agent with fixed metric tools and an MCP server lets marketers and their own agents ask 'why did we drop?' instead of reading charts.
First-party grounding data
Bing Webmaster AI performance topics and AI referral traffic in GA4 add real demand signals next to sampled answers.
Batch APIs for parsing
Parsing is not latency-critical: provider batch APIs (about half price) plus a small model keep cost per answer low.
Shopping and ads in answers
AI answers now include product carousels, checkout and ads, so trackers parse products and prices, not just brand mentions.

extra.look: A search CTO wants to hear how you know the numbers are right before you scale them.
rounds: The same prompt gives a different answer 30 seconds later. What do you report?
A rate over N runs with a confidence interval
The best answer of the day
The first answer of the day
You improve the parser. What lets you fix last month's numbers?
Raw answers kept in object storage, then re-parse
Ask the engines again for last month
Adjust the old numbers by a fixed factor
Two tenants track the exact same prompt, engine and region today. What do you do?
Run it once and share the raw answer

modern: Wilson or Bayesian intervals
Small samples near 0% or 100% need intervals that stay inside 0-100% - Wilson or a Beta posterior.
Sequential testing
Stop sampling early when the answer is already clear, keep sampling when the interval straddles the alert threshold.
Control prompts
A fixed set of brand-neutral prompts detects engine-wide shifts so they are not blamed on a brand.

extra.look: They want honest numbers explained in one plain sentence.
rounds: 7 mentions in 10 runs. Best way to say it?
Visibility drops from 60% to 50% with 10 runs each. Alert?
No - the intervals overlap heavily, collect more runs
Yes, a 10 point drop is big
Yes, always alert on any drop
How do you halve the width of an interval?

modern: Agentic search
Engines plan several searches, judge if they have enough, and search again - fan-out within one answer.
Learned sparse + dense
Learned sparse models (SPLADE, ELSER) sit next to BM25 and vectors in hybrid retrieval.
Late interaction
ColBERT-style token-level matching catches compound queries that one vector per page averages away.
Cheap vector storage
Object-storage-backed vector indexes make the database a commodity; retrieval quality is the product.

extra.look: Expect follow-ups on BM25, hybrid fusion and rerankers from a long-time Elasticsearch engineer.
rounds: A user asks for a CRM that integrates with Bitbucket AND Slack. Which retriever most often misses it?
A single dense vector per page
Why fuse with RRF instead of adding scores?
BM25 and cosine scores live on different scales; ranks don't
It removes the need for a reranker
Where do you spend the expensive cross-encoder?
On every document in the index

modern: Code mode
Let the agent write a small script that calls many tools at once - fewer turns, fewer tokens.
Skills
Package playbooks as skills loaded on demand, so the context holds only what this task needs.
MCP for customers
The same typed tools exposed over MCP with OAuth scopes turn the product into a platform.

extra.look: They care about tenant isolation, evidence and evals for every agent answer.
rounds: Who chooses the tenant id in a tool call?
The server, from the authenticated session
A cited web page says 'ignore previous instructions'. What happens?
Nothing - retrieved text is data, never instructions
How do you know a new model made the agent better?
Re-run the eval set of real questions and compare

modern: Hyperbolic embeddings
Hierarchies fit curved (hyperbolic) space far better than flat vectors, but HNSW assumes flat space - prefetch many candidates and rescore.
Fan-out capture
Engines expose or leak the sub-queries they search; those are the real demand signals.
Multi-parent taxonomies
Store topics as a graph of tags, not one tree, so a prompt can live under pricing AND integrations.

extra.look: They want measured thresholds, not magic numbers.
rounds: How do you choose the duplicate threshold?
Label pairs, sweep the threshold, pick by precision
Topic ids change every re-cluster. Fix?
Match new clusters to old by centroid and keep ids
Searching prompts for 'HubSpot pricing' - best retriever?
Hybrid: BM25 for the name plus vectors

modern: Signed bot traffic
Web Bot Auth and verified bot lists from CDNs make bot identity cryptographic, not just a user agent.
Pay per crawl
CDNs let sites charge or block AI crawlers per request - a new signal to track.
Agent traffic
AI agents browsing on a user's behalf (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User) behave like humans and may not follow robots.txt.

extra.look: Volume, verification and columnar storage.
rounds: Best proof a hit really is GPTBot?
Its IP is in OpenAI's published ranges
Big batches, about one insert per second

modern: llms.txt
A markdown index at /llms.txt points AI tools at the clean versions of key pages.
Markdown for agents at the CDN
CDNs can convert HTML to markdown for AI agents on request, no app code needed.
Structured data
schema.org markup in both versions gives engines clean facts to lift.

extra.look: They wrote this system - expect sharp questions on caching and honesty.
rounds: Rewrite - the URL (and citation) stays the real page
Humans start getting markdown. Likely cause?
The cache key ignores bot vs human
How do you show it works?
A/B over page groups, compare citation rates

modern: AI bot access checks
Check robots.txt for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended separately - they do different jobs.
Render budgets
Headless rendering only when needed, from a pooled browser farm.
Liftable facts
Small models flag pages where key facts are buried in images, tabs or vague copy.

extra.look: Classic crawler questions with an AI search twist.
rounds: One queue and rate limit per domain
Rarely skipping a page we never fetched
Only when raw HTML lacks the main content

modern: LLM judges at scale
Calibrated LLM judges label thousands of query-document pairs cheaply, with humans auditing a sample.
Error analysis first
Read ~100 real failures, group them into a failure taxonomy, then build metrics for the biggest groups.

extra.look: A relevance engineer will test whether you pick the right metric for the stage.
rounds: Metric for the final top 10 order?
Why interleaving over A/B for rankers?
It needs much less traffic to see a difference

modern: Code mode
Agents write one small program that calls many tools - fewer turns, fewer tokens, higher recall.
Trained search agents
Models trained to search raise recall but can lower precision - keep a reranker.

extra.look: Turns, tokens and stopping rules.
rounds: Why do fewer turns save money?
Each turn re-sends the growing context
Judge coverage of each sub-question plus hard caps
Evidence recall on questions with known sources

modern: Shadow traffic
Run the new pipeline on mirrored inputs with no customer impact before any cutover.
Feature flags per tenant
Cut over and roll back one tenant at a time.

extra.look: They just bought a company - this may be live work.
rounds: Old and new disagree. Who decides?
Hand-labelled samples of the raw answers
How to stop a cliff in customer charts?
Backfill history and annotate the cutover
Cut over all tenants at once

modern: Cascaded voice is back in favour
Streaming speech-to-text, a model, then streaming text-to-speech gives more control and debuggability than one speech-to-speech model; frameworks like LiveKit Agents handle turns and barge-in.
Word-timed interruptions
TTS returns word timings, so after a barge-in the agent keeps only the words the learner actually heard.
Generative UI from typed actions
Agents place known components through schema-checked actions instead of writing HTML; canvas kits (tldraw's agent starter) stream each action as it completes.
Model per job + fast classifiers
A small classifier routes and grades with stable, confidence-scored answers; big models only where they earn it.
Agents with memory and skills
Deep-agent harnesses add planning, sub-agents, skills loaded on demand and a long-term memory store.
Evals as the release gate
Consistency tests, online evaluators and human review queues decide what ships.

extra.look: They want a latency budget, an interruption story and a clear line between what runs live and what runs in the background.
rounds: Where should the expensive planning model run?
In a background workflow, never on the live voice turn
The learner interrupts. What must the agent remember?
Only the words that were actually played before the interruption
Nothing - start a new turn blank
How should the tutor change the canvas?
Typed, schema-checked actions on a known component catalog
Model writes raw HTML into the page
Grading drifts run to run. First fix?
Split the rubric into one question per criterion and score each with a stable classifier, then test consistency
Ask the model to be consistent

scenarios.name: Onboarding tutor at work
scenarios.blurb: Teach a new hire a team's own systems from its docs and tickets.
scenarios.lens: Permissions, grounding and adoption inside a company's own tools.
reqF: Answer from the team's docs and tickets with citations
Start automatically on a new-hire event
reqN: Never show a page the learner can't open
Writes to tickets only as drafts a person approves
dives: How do you ground lessons in the company's knowledge?
Search the company's own docs and tickets with the learner's own permissions, and cite the real pages so the learner can check them.
How do you prove value after 12 weeks?
Time-to-first-ticket for new hires, questions deflected from senior engineers, and review pass rates - measured against a baseline from Discover.
wrap: Next: event triggers for every new joiner, and a shared course library per team.

scenarios.name: Exam prep at scale
scenarios.blurb: 100k learners revising before the same exam date.
scenarios.lens: Peak load, cost per learner and fair grading.
est: Peak: 100k concurrent in the final week = 100k rooms; pre-warm agent workers and reserve model capacity
dives: The night before the exam traffic spikes 20x. What protects you?
Autoscaled stateless agent workers, per-learner quotas, a kill switch, small models on the hot path and cached system prompts.
wrap: Next: exam-board aligned rubrics and teacher dashboards.

scenarios.name: Kids mode
scenarios.blurb: Children aged 8-12 learning maths.
reqN: No recording by default; parent consent first
Stricter guardrails and topic allow-list
dives: What changes for children?
A policy profile turns off recordings and long-term memory by default, tightens guardrails, adds parental consent and reports, and a DPIA is done before launch.
wrap: Next: teacher-assigned courses and classroom view.

modern: Grounding on a work graph
Agents follow relationships between tickets, pages, code and people instead of searching flat documents; vendors report better accuracy with fewer tokens.
Permission-aware retrieval as a hard rule
ACLs are ingested with the data and enforced at query time, with a second check against the source.
Hybrid LLM pipelines
A different model per stage: small models for routing and rewriting, strong ones for answers, each with its own eval set.
Event-triggered agents
Agents start on business events and run inside automations, so throttling and queues matter as much as prompts.
MCP and CLI access to company context
The same graph is exposed to outside assistants and coding agents through MCP servers and CLIs.
Plans for approval
Reasoning modes show the plan first and wait for a person before writing to systems.

extra.look: They want permissions designed in from the start, a clear write-approval story, and a way to prove value to the customer.
rounds: At retrieval inside the index, then again against the source before the model sees anything
A user isn't mapped to a company identity. What do they see?
Nothing from that source - fail closed
Whatever the connector account can see
Which tools can an automation-triggered agent run by default?
Read tools; writes need approval or a scoped rule
How do you know an answer change helped?
Offline evals on a fixed set plus the online success rate, one stage changed at a time
Ask the model if it improved

scenarios.name: Rollout for one big customer
scenarios.blurb: Deploy the agent for one customer's teams in 12 weeks.
scenarios.lens: One workflow, a baseline metric, adoption and a reusable pattern.
reqF: Pick one high-value workflow with the customer (e.g. incident triage)
Connect the customer's own system with a custom connector
reqN: Ship value in 12 weeks with a measured baseline
Leave the pattern reusable for the next team
dives: How do you choose the first workflow?
High volume, clear owner, measurable today (time to triage, questions to senior engineers), low write risk. Start Read-only, add Draft, then Act.
The customer's admin blocks agents in automations. Plan B?
The agent still answers; downstream steps use its response text (agentResponse) and a person applies the change.
wrap: Next: turn the engagement into a reusable template and feedback to the product team.

scenarios.name: Regulated bank
scenarios.blurb: Same agent where every answer can be audited.
scenarios.lens: Data residency, audit and least privilege.
reqN: Data stays in region; admin allow/block lists for each connector
Every answer stores its sources and the ACL check result
dives: An auditor asks why the agent showed a document. What can you show?
The audit record: question, retrieved items, both permission checks with their results, the model and prompt version, and the approver for any write.
wrap: Next: per-tenant keys and residency, red-team evals for data leakage.

scenarios.name: Startup on day one
scenarios.blurb: 200 people, Slack, Google Drive and GitHub, no platform team.
scenarios.lens: Use managed pieces; keep it simple.
est: 200 people x ~5 questions/day = ~1k queries/day: one Postgres with pgvector and a managed reranker is plenty
dives: What do you not build?
No custom index cluster or graph database yet: managed search, one database, and a gateway with quotas. Add the graph when relationship questions show up.
wrap: Next: add connectors as tools grow; move to a dedicated index past a few million chunks.

production-agent-platform.stackNote: How LangChain's Managed Deep Agents does it (Interrupt London talk + docs)
modern: Agent = model + harness
Frameworks now ship a base harness (planning, filesystem, sub-agents, skills, memory, approvals) that teams customise for their domain.
Context engineering over prompt engineering
Offload, compact, select and isolate context so long runs stay on track.
Durable runs with human steering
Checkpoints after each step let agents pause for approvals or sign-ins and resume days later.
Identity-aware agents
Who called the agent decides which credentials and memories it can use.
Evals in real environments
Agents are scored on tasks inside sandboxes with verifiers, not single prompts.
Agents that schedule themselves
Agents create their own recurring runs and work from many channels.

extra.look: They want you to separate business logic, harness and infrastructure, and explain context management and identity clearly.
rounds: A tool returns 200k tokens of logs. What does the harness do?
Save it to the agent's filesystem and keep a short pointer in the prompt
Put it all in the prompt
The agent is used in a shared Slack channel. Which credentials?
Agent-scoped service account, and no private memories
A run waits 3 days for a user to approve. What holds it?
A saved checkpoint; no process is waiting
A cron job polling every second
Best first step to make a team's agent better?
Turn their expertise into skills and build evals on their real tasks

scenarios.name: Internal agents for a customer
scenarios.blurb: Stand up agents for a large customer's teams in the tools they already use.
scenarios.lens: One team, one workflow, scoped identity, adoption.
reqF: Agents live in the ticket tracker, the wiki and chat where the team already works
Start from events (new ticket, incident) as well as chat
dives: How do you map this onto a customer's own platform?

Find their equivalents: their agent framework is the harness, their app platform is the runtime, their search or work graph is the context and permission layer, their automation is the trigger, and actions run as the user or as an app. The principles stay: who is calling decides access, and writes need approval.
wrap: Next: package the agent as a reusable template for the customer's next team.

scenarios.name: The AI Voice Tutor's planner
scenarios.blurb: Background agents that build a learner's course while the voice tutor talks.
scenarios.lens: Background runs, per-learner memory, approvals from a teacher.
dives: How does the planner run without slowing the voice turn?
It runs as a queued background run with its own checkpoints; the live tutor only reads the finished plan from memory. Teachers can approve the course through an interrupt.
wrap: Next: per-learner schedules created by the agent ("review fractions on Friday").

modern: AI moderators at scale
Products now run 1,000s of 1:1 video interviews in parallel, in dozens of languages, with adaptive follow-ups - qualitative depth at survey speed.
Evidence-linked insights
Every chart and theme links back to the verbatim and the clip, so stakeholders trust AI-made reports.
Always-on research
Instead of one-off projects, scheduled waves feed a growing knowledge base that teams query in plain English.
MCP for research data
Research tools expose MCP servers so assistants like Claude can query interview data directly.
Enterprise AI hosting
Big customers ask for EU hosting, dedicated model deployments and a promise that their data never trains models.

extra.look: They want to see how a stakeholder can check any claim, and how the system avoids invented quotes and shaky numbers.
rounds: How should the coder return a quote?
As a span (offsets) inside the transcript, verified before use
As free text the model writes
As a summary of the answer
As a screenshot of the transcript
A theme shows '58%' from 12 people. Best fix?
Show the count with a range and flag the small base
Ask the model for a better number
Where should the interview flow live?
In code as a state machine; the model only phrases and decides to probe
A prompt change might shift old results. What do you store?
The prompt and model version on every result

scenarios.name: Global brand, many markets
scenarios.blurb: A consumer brand runs the same study in 7 markets and 10 languages.
scenarios.lens: Languages, translation and comparable results across markets.
reqF: Interview in the participant's language; report in the team's language
reqN: Same guide, comparable codes in every market

blocks.tl: Store the original transcript and a translation into the reporting language; code on the translation, quote the original.

dives: Code in the original language or the translation?
Code on one reporting language so codes compare across markets, but always keep and show the original quote next to the translation.
wrap: Next: per-market evals and local panel partners.

scenarios.name: First version in 6 weeks
scenarios.blurb: A small team ships the first paying version.
scenarios.lens: Managed services, simple choices, fast iteration.
est: 10 customers, 2k interviews/month: one Postgres, one queue, managed transcription
dives: What would you not build yet?
Live streaming voice, custom models and multi-region. Start with record-per-answer, managed speech-to-text, Postgres + a job queue, and one region.
wrap: Next: add the knowledge base once customers have run several studies.

scenarios.name: Health and pharma research
scenarios.blurb: Patients and doctors interviewed about treatments.
reqN: Consent recorded before any recording
Audit log of every view of a recording

blocks.red: Redact names, numbers and health details before any model sees the transcript; raw media locked down with short retention.

dives: What changes for health research?
Explicit consent capture, redaction before analysis, stricter retention, access logs on media, region-locked processing and a DPIA before launch.
wrap: Next: adverse-event detection that alerts a human.

modern: Cascaded voice with streaming
Streaming speech-to-text, a model and text-to-speech give control and debuggability; frameworks such as LiveKit Agents handle turns and interruptions.
Small models for decisions
A fast classifier decides 'probe or move on' with a confidence; bigger models only phrase.
Simulated participants for testing
Persona-driven synthetic participants test a guide before real people see it.
Real people on camera, no avatars
Showing the question as text and voice often feels more natural than an animated face.

extra.look: They want a clear rule for when to dig deeper and when to move on, within the time budget.
rounds: The answer is 'it was fine'. What next?
Probe once with a neutral open question about why
Ask three follow-ups in a row
The section is out of time. What wins?
The guide's time budget: move on
Where does 'probe or not' get decided?
A small classifier with a typed yes/no and a reason
The biggest model on every turn

scenarios.name: Answer any time (async)
scenarios.blurb: People record each answer when it suits them, on a phone.
scenarios.lens: Simplicity and reliability over real-time feel.
reqN: Works on weak mobile data
Next question within ~2 s of upload
dives: What changes without live streaming?
Each answer is recorded and uploaded in chunks; the moderator decides the next question after the upload; there is no barge-in, and speech-to-text runs on the finished answer.
wrap: Next: add live mode for methods that need conversation.

scenarios.name: Usability with screen share
scenarios.blurb: Participants try a prototype while talking.
scenarios.lens: What is on screen shapes the follow-up.

blocks.scr: Screen events (page, clicks, time stuck) give the moderator context for the next question.

dives: How does the moderator use the screen?
Send compact events (page, element, time on step) - not video frames - to the decider, so it can ask 'what did you expect when you clicked that?'
wrap: Next: vision model summaries of key moments.

modern: Direct-to-storage uploads
Presigned multipart uploads keep app servers out of the byte path.
Managed media services
Managed transcoding and transcription replace self-run GPU and FFmpeg fleets for most teams.
Word-level timestamps everywhere
Modern speech-to-text returns word timings and speakers, so every quote is instantly a clip.

extra.look: They want retries that never double-process and a clear story for bad files.
rounds: A transcode job runs twice. What keeps it safe?
A unique job key and deterministic output keys
Deleting the second output by hand
One corrupt file keeps failing. What happens?
After a few tries it goes to a dead letter queue with an alert

scenarios.name: EU data residency
scenarios.blurb: An EU customer needs media to stay in the EU.
reqN: Storage and processing in the EU region only
dives: How do you keep media in-region?
Per-tenant region in config, a bucket and worker pool per region, routing by tenant, and transcription vendors with EU processing.
wrap: Next: per-tenant encryption keys.

modern: Typed outputs
Structured outputs and schemas make model results checkable and stable.
Batch APIs and prompt caching
Coding thousands of answers runs at batch prices with the codebook cached.
LLM-as-judge, calibrated
A judge model scales evaluation only after it agrees with human coders.

extra.look: They want codes you can audit and counts you can defend.
rounds: How do you check the coder before shipping?
Measure it against a golden set coded by researchers
Ask it if it is confident
Theme names change on every re-run. Fix?
Match themes to the last run by members and keep ids stable
Rename them by hand each time

scenarios.name: Weekly waves
scenarios.blurb: The same study runs every week for a year.
dives: How do themes stay comparable week to week?
Freeze the codebook, code new answers against it, propose new codes separately for review, and show changes only beyond the sample-size range.
wrap: Next: alerts when a theme grows.

modern: Agentic retrieval
Agents plan sub-queries and choose between search and structured queries.
MCP servers
Products expose read-only tools so customers' own assistants can ask questions.
Evidence over eloquence
Answers show the quotes and the base size, and say when evidence is thin.

extra.look: They want permission checks inside retrieval and a plan for counting questions.
rounds: Where do you apply study permissions?
Inside the search query, from the session identity
A query over the coded theme counts
Vector search and let the model count

scenarios.name: Customers' agents ask too
scenarios.blurb: Customer AI assistants query research through MCP.
dives: How do you open this safely to other agents?
Per-customer scoped tokens, read-only tools, the same permission filters, rate limits and usage metering, and citations in every answer.
wrap: Next: webhooks when new evidence arrives.
